headline: Bus, truck, and launch fares increased after fuel price hike, adding pressure on people
summary: Following a recent fuel price hike, bus fares have risen by 17 poisha per kilometer, with launch fares increasing by 17-20%. This surge in transport costs is directly impacting daily expenses and commodity prices for the public.
details: The government has increased bus fares by 17 poisha per kilometer, following a recent hike in fuel prices. Launch owners have also announced a 17-20% increase in fares per kilometer, while truck drivers are charging higher rates.

This collective increase in transportation costs, for the second time in five months, is putting renewed pressure on people and leading to higher prices for essential commodities. The burden of increased passenger fares falls directly on the public, while higher goods transport costs are eventually passed on to consumers in the market.

The government raised fuel prices by BDT 20 per liter on Sunday night. This follows a previous increase of BDT 15 to BDT 20 per liter in April, which also led to an 11 poisha per kilometer increase in bus fares and higher truck fares.

In total, diesel prices have risen by BDT 35 per liter over two phases in five months. Since almost all passenger vehicles (buses, trains, launches) and goods vehicles (trucks, covered vans) run on diesel, this price hike impacts all segments of society, including agricultural machinery operators.

Road Transport, Rail, and Shipping Minister Sheikh Rabiul Alam stated that while any fare increase is a burden, they managed to keep the current increases below what would be justified by the fuel price hike, considering the situation.

According to the new government notification, bus fares in Dhaka and Chattogram metropolitan areas have increased from BDT 2.53 to BDT 2.70 per kilometer. Minibus fares rose from BDT 2.43 to BDT 2.60 per kilometer, and long-haul 52-seater bus fares increased from BDT 2.23 to BDT 2.40 per kilometer.

The government does not regulate fares for air-conditioned (AC) buses or other goods vehicles like trucks and covered vans. However, instances of overcharging were observed on various routes even before the new official fare lists were fully implemented.

Passengers at Sayedabad and Fulbaria bus terminals reported paying BDT 50 to BDT 200 extra for long-haul buses. Within Dhaka, some local bus routes saw fares increase from BDT 10 to BDT 15, and from BDT 15 to BDT 20, though some buses maintained old fares until midday.

Ride-sharing motorcycle drivers are also charging an additional BDT 20 to BDT 50, depending on the distance. Drivers like Sabbir Hossain note that while passengers are reluctant to pay more, increased fuel costs leave them with no other option.

Truck drivers are also facing significant cost increases. Mohammad Masud, a truck driver, estimates an additional BDT 4,400 in diesel costs for a round trip between Pabna and Chattogram due to the BDT 20 per liter hike.

The Bangladesh Covered Van-Truck-Prime Mover Goods Transport Owners Association reported that truck owners are now demanding BDT 4,000 to BDT 6,000 more for certain routes. For example, transporting garments from Benapole to Dhaka's Kanchpur now costs BDT 22,000, up from BDT 18,000-19,000.

headline: DU student forced to return home due to poverty
summary: Alamin Hossain, a first-year student at Dhaka University, had to leave the capital after five months because his family cannot afford the costs of living and studying.
details: Alamin Hossain, a first-year student at the Institute of Social Welfare and Research at Dhaka University, has returned to his village in Kushtia after five months of struggling to stay in Dhaka.
caption:
A dream shattered by poverty: a Dhaka University student returns home because he cannot afford to live in the capital.

Alamin Hossain, a first-year student at the Institute of Social Welfare and Research at Dhaka University, has returned to his village in Kushtia after five months of struggling to stay in Dhaka.
